newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks firm late on index-linked demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks firm late on index-linked demand.

text.p: Singapore shares ended on a firm note on Monday, helped by institutional demand for blue chip stocks after a bullish run in Wall Street, dealers said.
They said trade picked in the afternoon session with multimedia, technology and electronic counters drawing attention and gathered further momentum late in the day on index-related stock buying.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rose 21.64 points to end at the session's high of 2,245.72.
Total volume was moderate at 132 million lots with gainers outpacing losers by 342 to 46.
Strength in regional bourses and the second board market also provided momentum, dealers said.
"There was much sought-after blue chip buying following the Dow's rally," one brokerage dealer said, but noted that volume was still thin at the start of the new year.
Among net gain leaders were Singapore Press foreign, up Singapore $0.70 to S$28.40 and foreign tranches of OUB, up $0.50 to $11.10 and OCBC, up $0.30 to $17.90.
Multimedia company Aztech dominated actives again with 12.65 million shares and rose S$0.075 to S$0.56.
